snp5.5:1.1: I ask you, Blessed One. Please tell me.

snp5.5:2.1: The Buddha: You ask me the source of stress.
snp5.5:2.3: I’ll tell it to you as one who discerns.
snp5.5:2.5: the many forms of stress come into being in the world.
snp5.5:3.2: —the dullard— comes to stress again & again.
snp5.5:3.3: Therefore, discerning, you shouldn’t create acquisitions
snp5.5:3.4: as you stay focused on the birth & origin of stress.

snp5.5:4.2: Now we ask something else. Please tell us.

snp5.5:5.5: you’ll cross over beyond entanglement in the world.

snp5.5:7.5: Dispelling any delight, any entrenchment in those things, consciousness should not take a stance in becoming.

snp5.5:9.1: Mettagū: I relish, Gotama, the Great Seer’s words

snp5.5:10.1: And they, too, would abandon stress those whom you, sage, would admonish unceasingly.
snp5.5:10.3: Having met you, I bow down to you, Nāga.

snp5.5:11.1: The Buddha: Whoever you recognize as a brahman, an attainer-of-knowledge
snp5.5:11.2: possessing nothing, unentangled in sensuality & becoming—
snp5.5:11.3: yes, he has crossed over this flood.
snp5.5:11.4: Having crossed to the far shore, he’s free from rigidity, free from doubt.
snp5.5:12.1: And anyone who has realized, who is an attainer-of-knowledge here,
snp5.5:12.2: having unentangled the bond to becoming and non-,
snp5.5:12.4: he, I tell you, has crossed over birth & aging.
